videos.title: पहले यह जान लो: tissue समझने के जरूरी tools
videos.goal: आप cell के जरूरी हिस्से, division के basic words, body और plant के landmarks तथा transport, support और control के सीधे meanings को छोटे examples से समझ सकेंगे।
prerequisites_taught: Cell boundaries, organelles and plant–animal cell differences
Chromosomes, homologous pairs, chromatids, DNA replication and chromosome sets
Somatic cells, germ cells, gametes and fertilisation
Locations and roles of the named human organs, passages and skeleton
Diffusion, absorption, secretion and movement through walls or pores
Photosynthesis, food storage and the functions of structural biological materials
Physical meanings of tension, elasticity, pressure, buoyancy and insulation
Stimulus, nerve impulse, electrical signal and voluntary versus involuntary control
videos.opening_hook: एक ही शरीर में skin ढकती है, muscle खींचता है और nerve message पहुँचाती है—इनको समझने से पहले cell में क्या पहचानना जरूरी है?
videos.story_or_analogy: छोटे visual examples: कमरे की boundary से membrane और wall का फर्क, खिंचे rubber से elasticity, पानी पर तैरती चीज से buoyancy और गरम कपड़े से insulation। हर analogy की सीमा बताई जाएगी; यह बाहर का standard textbook-level support है।
videos.why_this_unit: Cell sketch, chromosome-pair sketch, body–plant locator और everyday physical examples से हर prerequisite को meaning तथा example मिलेगा। Replication में DNA बढ़ने और chromosome sets बदलने को अलग समझाया जाएगा; organelles या reproduction का पूरा पुराना chapter नहीं खुलेगा।

videos.title: Cells मिलकर tissue कैसे बनाते हैं?
videos.goal: आप division of labour से tissue, organ, organ system और organism का रिश्ता समझेंगे; mitosis–meiosis तथा plant–animal mitosis को book के सभी comparison criteria पर अलग कर सकेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: चोट के बाद skin ठीक होती है, लेकिन बच्चे बनने की प्रक्रिया में chromosome number आधा करना क्यों जरूरी होता है?
videos.story_or_analogy: अलग काम करने वाली teams मिलकर एक काम पूरा करती हैं—इससे division of labour समझेंगे, फिर cell से organism तक असली biological levels पर लौटेंगे।
videos.why_this_unit: Organisation के बाद cells की संख्या और उनके बनने का तरीका स्वाभाविक अगला सवाल है। दोनों comparisons में common basis, हर criterion के दोनों पक्ष और recap table आएँगे; DNA replication को chromosome-number doubling समझने की गलती साफ अलग की जाएगी।

videos.title: Animal tissues: शरीर में कौन क्या करता है?
videos.goal: आप 4 primary animal-tissue groups और book में दिए connective subgroups का tree बना सकेंगे तथा body diagram में tissue, जगह और काम जोड़ सकेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: आपके हाथ की skin, उसके नीचे की चर्बी, muscle और nerve—क्या ये सब एक ही तरह का tissue हैं?
videos.story_or_analogy: हाथ से शुरुआत करके body diagram में बाहर से अंदर जाएँगे: covering, जोड़ने-सहारा देने वाला material, movement और message।
videos.why_this_unit: Classification tree को human-body locator के साथ पढ़ने से नाम जगह और function से जुड़ेंगे। हर group के समान परिचय-slots, मुख्य फर्क और छोटा memory cue होगा; बाद के videos इन्हीं branches को खोलेंगे। Figure के हर label को तय reading path से पढ़ेंगे।

videos.title: Epithelial tissue: covering की बनावट काम कैसे बदलती है?
videos.goal: आप epithelial sheets, barriers और gland formation समझेंगे; book के हर epithelial type को layers, shape, special feature, location तथा function से पहचानेंगे और drawings में true तथा apparent stratification अलग करेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: Skin को बचाव करना है और lung air sacs को gases पार होने देनी हैं—क्या दोनों जगह एक जैसी covering चलेगी?
videos.story_or_analogy: पतली exchange boundary और कई layers वाले protective cover की तुलना केवल thickness–function link समझाने के लिए होगी; हर निष्कर्ष असली tissue और book के location पर लौटेगा।
videos.why_this_unit: Sheet की common structure के बाद पूरा epithelial family tree आएगा। हर member समान slots में खुलेगा, फिर उसका drawing और location zoom होगा। अंत में confused pairs, side-by-side comparison, memory cue और matching-style check होगा।

videos.title: Connective tissue: matrix से support, storage और transport तक
videos.goal: आप matrix और fibres से connective tissues के गुण समझेंगे; book की सभी varieties, locations तथा atlas labels पहचानेंगे और subcutaneous fat वाले HPAS 2020 question का कारण सहित उत्तर दे सकेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: Blood बहता है और bone सख्त होती है—फिर दोनों connective tissue कैसे हैं?
videos.story_or_analogy: Cells के आसपास का material बदलने से tissue का व्यवहार बदलता है। खिंचाव और वापस लौटने के छोटे demonstrations collagen तथा elastic fibres का फर्क खोलेंगे।
videos.why_this_unit: Common matrix–fibre structure से varieties की properties निकलेंगी। Overview के बाद हर member की structure, नाम का आधार जहाँ book देता है, feature, function और location पढ़ेंगे। Atlas में Haversian canals, canaliculi, chondrocytes, adipocytes और blood-cell labels पहचानेंगे; अंत में fat से कम heat loss की cause chain और supplied PYQ करेंगे।

videos.title: Muscle और nerve: खिंचाव, control और message का रास्ता
videos.goal: आप contraction से movement का रिश्ता, skeletal–smooth–cardiac muscle का पूरा comparison, tendon attachment और neuron में impulse की direction समझेंगे; striation को voluntary control का प्रमाण नहीं मानेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: आप हाथ उठाना रोक सकते हैं, लेकिन heartbeat को उसी तरह रोकने का आदेश क्यों नहीं दे सकते?
videos.story_or_analogy: हाथ मोड़ने का familiar action contraction, bone और tendon को जोड़ेगा। Neuron के लिए message का रास्ता केवल direction समझाने का सहारा होगा, biological mechanism का विकल्प नहीं।
videos.why_this_unit: पहले contraction का result, जगह और book में दिया mechanism; फिर 3-member muscle tree और हर member के समान structure–location–function slots होंगे। Comparison में branching, striation, nuclei और control अलग criteria रहेंगे। Cardiac question तथा tendon–ligament–cartilage distinction के बाद अलग neuron भाग में parts, synapse और arrows का reading path होगा। हर भाग का recap और अंत में एक closing recap होगा।

videos.title: Plant tissues का पूरा family tree
videos.goal: आप book के पूरे plant-tissue hierarchy को division के आधार सहित पढ़ सकेंगे और हर branch तथा member की जगह पहचान सकेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: पेड़ की बढ़ती नोक, मुलायम पत्ती और सख्त तना—इन अलग कामों को एक tissue map में कैसे रखेंगे?
videos.story_or_analogy: एक family tree में पहले बड़ी branches, फिर छोटी branches खोलेंगे; plant के familiar हिस्से हर branch का location anchor होंगे।
videos.why_this_unit: Pages 1 और 8 के classification material को एक जगह जोड़ना जरूरी है। हर division का आधार, सभी named members, book में दिए distinguishing features, comparison और memory cue यहीं पढ़ेंगे। आगे के videos इसी tree की structures और mechanisms खोलेंगे, classification फिर से नहीं दोहराएँगे।

videos.title: Plant कहाँ बढ़ता है और cells specialised कैसे बनते हैं?
videos.goal: आप meristematic cells की features, apical–lateral–intercalary locations और length–girth effects समझेंगे; supplied statements हल करेंगे और differentiation से permanent tissue बनने की प्रक्रिया समझेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: पौधे की ऊँचाई बढ़ना और तने का मोटा होना—क्या दोनों का growth point एक ही जगह होता है?
videos.story_or_analogy: Plant sketch पर tip, base और side को अलग रंग से track करेंगे, ताकि location से growth effect निकले, केवल नाम याद न करना पड़े।
videos.why_this_unit: Meristem types को समान cell-feature, location और growth-effect slots में compare करेंगे। तुरंत supplied location question से गलत pairing जाँचेंगे। फिर dividing cell से specialised permanent tissue तक book की differentiation sequence, उसकी conditions और result पढ़ेंगे।

videos.title: Simple permanent tissues: storage, flexibility और strength
videos.goal: आप parenchyma और उसकी specialisations, collenchyma तथा sclerenchyma को structure से function तक समझेंगे; living contents, walls, spaces और locations पर compare करके buoyancy वाले questions हल करेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: मुलायम plant part, बिना टूटे मुड़ने वाला हिस्सा और सख्त seed covering—इनमें support का तरीका अलग क्यों है?
videos.story_or_analogy: मुड़ते plant part और कठोर covering को साथ देखकर flexibility तथा rigidity का फर्क खोलेंगे। Air spaces से floating का छोटा visual aerenchyma समझाएगा।
videos.why_this_unit: Simple permanent tissue की पूरी family एक साथ रहेगी। Overview tree के बाद हर member के समान slots, chlorenchyma–aerenchyma का function difference, wall thickening से support की cause chains और सभी comparative drawings पढ़ेंगे। सबसे confused pairs, full comparison table, memory cue और supplied practice अंत में होंगे।

videos.title: Xylem और phloem: components से transport समझें
videos.goal: आप complex tissue का मतलब, xylem और phloem के सभी components, उनके काम, labelled drawings और stem arrangement समझेंगे; living–dead exceptions तथा non-xylem component question सही करेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: जड़ों से पानी और पत्तियों से बना food बाकी plant तक पहुँचता है—क्या दोनों के लिए एक जैसी transport line होती है?
videos.story_or_analogy: Transport network का visual अलग materials और routes समझाने में मदद करेगा; storage तथा support करने वाले components को भी दिखाएँगे, ताकि हर component को केवल pipe न मानें।
videos.why_this_unit: Whole vascular bundle से components तक zoom करेंगे। Xylem और phloem members के समान structure–function slots, diagrams के सारे labels और stem में arrangement के बाद side-by-side comparison आएगा। Xylem parenchyma तथा phloem fibres जैसे exceptions स्पष्ट होंगे; printed transport shortcuts को absolute rules नहीं बनाएँगे।

videos.title: Plant की protective covering और gas exchange: questions खोलकर समझें
videos.goal: आप protective covering को wall material से और stomatal pore को guard cells से अलग कर सकेंगे; supplied questions के हर option को कारण देकर जाँच सकेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: पत्ती की covering बचाव भी करती है और gases का आना-जाना भी होने देती है—यह दोनों काम साथ कैसे होते हैं?
videos.story_or_analogy: Covering में opening और उसे नियंत्रित करने वाले हिस्सों का visual इस्तेमाल करेंगे; pore और guard cells को एक ही चीज मानने की सीमा वहीं साफ होगी।
videos.why_this_unit: इन practice questions में नए explanatory links हैं, इसलिए इन्हें जल्दबाजी वाले final quiz में नहीं दबाएँगे। Plant से leaf covering और फिर pore–guard cells तक zoom, function से structure का रिश्ता और option-wise reasoning पढ़ेंगे। Book से बाहर जरूरी epidermis, wall-material या gas-exchange support को स्पष्ट रूप से बाहर का standard textbook explanation बताएँगे।

plan.chapter_flow: पहले 8 मिनट में सीधे जरूरी tools सीखेंगे। फिर organisation और cell division से animal-tissue tree बनेगा; epithelial, connective तथा muscle families अपने figures और questions सहित खुलेंगी, और neuron message की direction जोड़ेगा। इसके बाद plant-tissue tree से meristems, differentiation, simple permanent tissues और vascular tissues तक जाएँगे। आखिरी video protective covering तथा gas-exchange questions को समझाकर chapter बंद करेगा। सभी 35 concepts शामिल हैं; topic narration 100 मिनट और prerequisite सहित कुल 108 मिनट है। Topic videos prerequisites को अधिकतम 2 reminder beats में याद दिलाएँगे, दोबारा नहीं पढ़ाएँगे।

videos.title: पहले यह जान लो: tissue समझने के जरूरी tools

frame.process: Identify cell boundaries, internal contents and plant–animal differences.
frame.how: Move from membrane and wall to cytoplasm, nucleus and organelles.
frame.when: Before interpreting tissue cells and spaces.
frame.conditions: Typical plant and animal cells; specialised cells may differ.
frame.atmosphere: Two enlarged cells beside a familiar room-boundary image.

frame.process: Distinguish chromosomes, homologous partners, chromatids and sets.
frame.how: Follow DNA copying while keeping chromosome number separate from DNA quantity.
frame.when: Replication precedes division; copied chromatids later separate.
frame.conditions: Count chromosomes by centromeres; distinguish n from 2n.
frame.atmosphere: Paired instruction books and a simple chromosome diagram.

frame.process: Distinguish body cells, reproductive cell lineage and gametes.
frame.how: Connect meiosis with reduction and fertilisation with restoration of chromosome sets.
frame.when: Gamete formation precedes fertilisation.
frame.conditions: Use the human reproductive context.
frame.atmosphere: A body-cell example beside sperm and egg joining.

frame.process: Locate the organs and passages named in tissue descriptions.
frame.how: Trace digestive, respiratory, urinary, circulatory and nervous routes, then support structures.
frame.when: Before zooming from organs to their tissue linings.
frame.conditions: Distinguish neighbouring passages and ducts by their destinations.
frame.atmosphere: A simple labelled human-body outline.

frame.process: Locate plant organs, stem regions and section landmarks.
frame.how: Move from the whole plant to nodes, coverings and a stem cross-section.
frame.when: Before locating growth and transport tissues.
frame.conditions: Separate lengthwise position from outside-to-inside position.
frame.atmosphere: A potted plant beside a cut stem and split seeds.

frame.process: Distinguish diffusion, absorption, secretion and passage through openings.
frame.how: Use movement direction, concentration difference and selective barriers.
frame.when: During exchange, uptake and release.
frame.conditions: Movement depends on the barrier and the substance; pores do not imply unrestricted passage.
frame.atmosphere: An intestinal lining, a gland and a magnified plant wall.

frame.process: Connect food production, storage and biological materials with their jobs.
frame.how: Separate substances from the tissues containing or producing them.
frame.when: During photosynthesis, storage, support and protection.
frame.conditions: Materials have different properties and are not interchangeable tissue names.
frame.atmosphere: A green leaf, stored food and contrasting biological coverings.

frame.process: Interpret pulling, recoil, pressure, floating and reduced heat loss.
frame.how: Connect each physical term to a visible everyday effect.
frame.when: During stretching, contraction, pumping, floating and cooling.
frame.conditions: Analogies illustrate properties, not identical biological mechanisms.
frame.atmosphere: A rope, rubber band, pump, floating object and warm clothing.

frame.process: Distinguish a stimulus, its nerve signal and conscious versus automatic control.
frame.how: Trace detection to signalling and response.
frame.when: After a detectable change or during ongoing automatic activity.
frame.conditions: Biological electrical signalling is not metal-wire conduction; appearance does not determine control.
frame.atmosphere: Touching something hot, raising a hand and feeling a heartbeat.

beats.say: कमरे के दरवाजे जैसा cell में आना-जाना कौन सँभालता है? Cell membrane चीजों का आना-जाना control करती है। Plant cell में इसके बाहर सहारा देने वाली cell wall भी होती है; animal cell में wall नहीं होती।

beats.say: Cell में ये छोटे हिस्से दिखे? Organelles अलग काम करते हैं; cytoplasm अंदर का substance है, nucleus में DNA की instructions हैं। Vacuole storage करती है, plant cell में अक्सर बड़ी होती है; chloroplast food बनाने में मदद करता है, लेकिन हर plant cell में नहीं होता।

beats.say: Skin cell और sperm का काम एक है? Somatic cells शरीर के सामान्य काम करती हैं; germ cells reproductive line की cells हैं। इंसान में sperm और egg gametes हैं; germ cell और mature gamete अलग stages हैं।

beats.say: पतली lining exchange का रास्ता छोटा करती है; microvilli उँगली जैसे उभार हैं, absorption का area बढ़ाते हैं। Permeability गुजरने देने की क्षमता है; wall pits पतले हिस्से, sieve plate pores रास्ते, stomata leaf openings हैं। हर रास्ते से हर चीज नहीं गुजरती।

beats.say: हरी पत्ती food बनाती है, आलू जमा करता है—कैसे? Photosynthesis में chlorophyll light पकड़ने में मदद करता है; plant carbon dioxide और water से sugars बनाता है। Food transport या store होता है; starch और fat energy reserves हैं।

frame.process: Identify a tissue by its shared cellular function.
frame.how: Start with arm movement, explain cooperation, and test mere proximity.
frame.when: Before classifying tissues.
frame.conditions: Cells must cooperate in a common function.
frame.atmosphere: A student watching an arm move.

frame.process: Separate plant and animal tissues by constituent cells.
frame.how: Compare a leaf with a human arm.
frame.when: After defining tissue.
frame.conditions: Origin determines these two broad categories, not layer count or shape.
frame.atmosphere: A leaf and an arm shown side by side.

frame.process: Explain division of labour and reduced individual workload.
frame.how: Connect specialised jobs to coordinated organisation.
frame.when: Once cooperating cell groups are established.
frame.conditions: Specialisation does not remove essential cellular functions.
frame.atmosphere: Teams sharing jobs rather than each doing everything.

skipped_steps.why: The source provides no separate experimental evidence; the concrete example illustrates the mechanism.

frame.process: Locate cells, tissues, organs and systems within a whole organism.
frame.how: Zoom inward through a human digestive example, then assemble the labelled hierarchy.
frame.when: Following the explanation of organisation.
frame.conditions: The hierarchy describes multicellular organisation, not every organism.
frame.atmosphere: Nested views of a human, digestive system, stomach, tissue and cell.

frame.process: Distinguish mitosis and meiosis across all printed criteria.
frame.how: Pair each criterion and correct the chromosome-replication error.
frame.when: Compare starting cells, divisions, products and chromosome outcomes.
frame.conditions: Diploid products assume a diploid mitotic starting cell; reproductive generalisations need qualification.
frame.atmosphere: Two branching division diagrams with separate chromosome-set and DNA counters.

frame.process: Compare typical plant and animal mitosis.
frame.how: Contrast division apparatus, cytoplasmic separation and locations.
frame.when: After distinguishing mitosis from meiosis.
frame.conditions: Plant statements describe typical higher plants; distributed animal division does not mean every cell divides.
frame.atmosphere: A root-tip cell beside a dividing animal cell.

frame.process: Organise animal tissues into four main groups and trace their subdivisions.
frame.how: Read from the root through each parent to its children.
frame.when: Read the main branches before their narrower categories; this is not a time sequence.
frame.conditions: Retain this book's classification scheme; lower branches are not extra primary groups.
frame.atmosphere: A classification tree linked to familiar skin, muscles, heart and blood.

frame.process: Distinguish the four tissue groups by their principal jobs.
frame.how: Compare covering, contraction, response and physical support using the same functional criteria.
frame.when: These tissues cooperate during an action rather than forming a developmental sequence.
frame.conditions: Primary functions distinguish groups; movement and signal response must not be conflated.
frame.atmosphere: A student considering the tissues involved in using a hand.

frame.process: Locate representative tissues and recognise their magnified forms.
frame.how: Follow the four panels from muscular to nerve to epithelial to connective tissue.
frame.when: Locate an organ or region, then inspect its representative tissue drawing.
frame.conditions: Pointers indicate associations, not flow routes or exclusive distributions.
frame.atmosphere: A central human body surrounded by magnified tissue examples.

videos.title: Epithelial tissue: covering की बनावट काम कैसे बदलती है?

frame.process: Epithelium forms continuous organ coverings and cavity linings.
frame.how: Closely packed cells with little intervening material lie over an extracellular fibrous basement membrane.
frame.when: Read the arrangement from the free surface down to underlying tissue.
frame.conditions: Continuity requires close packing; the supporting boundary is described as usually present.
frame.atmosphere: An enlarged side section of an organ lining.

frame.process: An epithelial barrier maintains separation between body compartments.
frame.how: A continuous sheet prevents unrestricted contact while suitable linings permit exchange.
frame.when: The boundary remains functional while compartment contents differ.
frame.conditions: Barrier does not mean impermeable to every substance.
frame.atmosphere: Gut contents on one side of a lining and underlying tissue on the other.

frame.process: Epithelial specialisation produces gland cells and sometimes multicellular glands.
frame.how: Cells acquire secretion capability; a portion of the sheet may fold inward.
frame.when: The inward fold precedes the described multicellular gland arrangement; it is an occasional route.
frame.conditions: Neither secretion nor inward folding is universal to all epithelial cells.
frame.atmosphere: An epithelial sheet folding inward beside a visible secretion.

skipped_steps.why: The source provides no failed gland-formation mechanism; adding one would invent content.

frame.process: Epithelial architectures support exchange, absorption, secretion, protection and changing liquid volume.
frame.how: Layer number, surface-cell shape, renewal, keratin and surface projections modify the lining.
frame.when: Read each tissue from its free surface inward; renewal and bladder stretching introduce temporal changes.
frame.conditions: Site lists are not uniform whole-organ claims; ciliation and keratinisation require separate checks.
frame.atmosphere: Matched sections of lung, kidney, gut, gland ducts, skin and urinary passages.

frame.process: Compare apparent epithelial layering with genuine stratification.
frame.how: Inspect unequal cell heights and trace contact with the basement membrane.
frame.when: Check actual layers before interpreting nuclear rows.
frame.conditions: Respiratory mucus clearance applies to ciliated examples, not every pseudostratified lining.
frame.atmosphere: Adjacent simple columnar, pseudostratified and truly stratified sections.

frame.process: Recognise epithelial forms in two sets of perspective drawings.
frame.how: Inspect true layers, surface-cell proportions and projections in a fixed reading path.
frame.when: Read the four-panel figure first, then the seven-form comparison.
frame.conditions: The figures are comparisons, not process sequences; nuclear height alone cannot establish layers.
frame.atmosphere: Labelled epithelial blocks viewed from the side and above.

beats.say: Tiles जैसी 1 पतली layer दिखे तो? Simple squamous है: flat cells की boundaries irregular हैं। Lungs के air sacs, blood vessels, capillaries और kidney की Bowman’s capsule में मिलता है; capsule यानी छोटी blood vessels के समूह के आसपास cup जैसी बनावट।

beats.say: Duct में कई layers और ऊपर cubes हों तो? Stratified Cuboidal है; नीचे दूसरी shapes भी हो सकती हैं। Mammary, यानी दूध बनाने वाली glands, sweat और salivary glands की ducts याद रखो; पूरी gland एक जैसी lining नहीं है।

videos.title: Connective tissue: matrix से support, storage और transport तक

frame.process: Connective tissue binds, supports and packs body structures through cells and extracellular material.
frame.how: Zoom from body connections to spaced cells, ground substance and three fibre types; tie each component to its mechanical role.
frame.when: The organisation is present continuously; elastic recoil follows removal of a stretching force.
frame.conditions: Composition and arrangement determine resistance to pulling, flexibility and recoil.
frame.atmosphere: A tissue field with scattered cells in gel and fibres, contrasted with an epithelial sheet.

frame.process: Support limits unwanted organ displacement, while fibres provide mechanical properties.
frame.how: Trace movement forces through supporting attachments and compare bending, tensile resistance and recoil.
frame.when: During body movement and during application or release of force.
frame.conditions: Normal movement remains possible; elasticity is not identical to flexibility or strength.
frame.atmosphere: A walking body alongside rope and rubber-band demonstrations.

frame.process: Matrix consistency varies across connective tissues.
frame.how: Compare jelly-like, fluid, dense and rigid material by behaviour and illustrative location.
frame.when: n/a: these are descriptive physical states, not successive stages.
frame.conditions: These descriptions are not necessarily mutually exclusive formal classes.
frame.atmosphere: Four material panels showing gel, flowing plasma, fibrous tendon and rigid bone.

frame.process: The definition identifies support and connection of tissues and organs.
frame.how: Build the definition from an attachment example, test its boundary and apply it to subsequent varieties.
frame.when: n/a: the definition has no temporal sequence.
frame.conditions: Shared identity does not require identical hardness or matrix consistency.
frame.atmosphere: Different organs held in a supported body arrangement.

frame.process: The figure locates cells, fibres, ground substance and a vessel within one tissue field.
frame.how: Read from upper left through the vessel and matrix annotation to the right-hand fibres and cells.
frame.when: n/a: leader lines identify structures rather than movement or stages.
frame.conditions: Drawing colours are conventions; the pictured vessel does not establish universal vascularity.
frame.atmosphere: The supplied description of the page-5 connective-tissue diagram.

frame.process: Connective-tissue varieties meet different support, transport, storage and protective needs.
frame.how: Compare location and function together, then explain the material properties behind those differences.
frame.when: During ordinary movement, breathing, circulation, injury and energy use.
frame.conditions: An organ can contain several tissue types; strength, rigidity, recoil and insulation are distinct properties.
frame.atmosphere: A body map linked to a tissue-location-function table.

frame.process: Five atlas panels make tissue and component identification concrete.
frame.how: Read blood, bone, cartilage, areolar and adipose panels in order, distinguishing cells from extracellular components.
frame.when: n/a: the panels are parallel examples, not developmental stages.
frame.conditions: Label position does not change tissue identity; fine bone channels differ from central canals.
frame.atmosphere: The five page-7 drawings with sequential label highlighting.

frame.process: Apply adipose insulation to the HPAS 2020 multiple-choice question.
frame.how: Identify the tested layer, select heat loss and distinguish each distractor's proposed function.
frame.when: When body heat would otherwise pass into cooler surroundings.
frame.conditions: Insulation slows heat transfer; storage and surface defence are different functions.
frame.atmosphere: An exam question beside a skin cross-section with outward heat arrows.

videos.title: Muscle और nerve: movement, control और message का रास्ता

frame.process: Muscle tissue generates pulling force through specialised cells.
frame.how: Zoom from tissue to elongated fibres and their internal contractile proteins.
frame.when: Establish the cellular structure before explaining activation.
frame.conditions: A muscle fibre is a cell, unlike an extracellular connective-tissue fibre.
frame.atmosphere: Picture the student's upper-arm muscle and a magnified fibre.

frame.process: Active muscle tension rises during contraction and falls during relaxation.
frame.how: Activation engages internal proteins; reduced activation lowers tension.
frame.when: Force generation and release alternate as movements require.
frame.conditions: Contraction need not visibly shorten a muscle; relaxation is not pushing.
frame.atmosphere: An arm grips, holds and releases an object.

frame.process: Identify the three branches of the muscle family.
frame.how: Introduce location, appearance and control as separate identifying criteria.
frame.when: Overview first; detailed member profiles follow in their assigned parts.
frame.conditions: A single shared feature cannot identify every muscle type.
frame.atmosphere: Arm, intestine and heart appear beside a three-branch family tree.

frame.process: Skeletal fibres develop force that reaches bones through attachments.
frame.how: Move from bone attachment to fibre outline, nuclei and internal bands.
frame.when: Describe the structural profile before its functions.
frame.conditions: Bone attachment is typical; multiple nuclei belong within one fibre.
frame.atmosphere: Upper arm and elbow beside a magnified cylindrical fibre.

frame.process: Skeletal muscle can lose force-producing capacity during effort.
frame.how: Explain the book's fatigue description through holding a heavy bag.
frame.when: During sustained or repeated demanding activity.
frame.conditions: Resistance varies with workload and muscle characteristics.
frame.atmosphere: A hand struggles to keep holding the same bag.

skipped_steps.why: The source gives no numerical magnitude to show to scale.

frame.process: Skeletal-muscle tension produces movement or stabilises posture.
frame.how: Trace pull through attachments to bones, then balance gravity without movement.
frame.when: During limb movement and while holding a body position.
frame.conditions: Muscles pull; opposing groups enable opposite movements.
frame.atmosphere: A bending elbow followed by a person standing upright.

frame.process: Interpret three descriptors of skeletal muscle.
frame.how: Separate attachment, banded appearance and conscious initiation.
frame.when: After the structure and function have been explained.
frame.conditions: The descriptors are not universally interchangeable categories.
frame.atmosphere: Three feature cards point to the same arm muscle.

frame.process: Read the skeletal-muscle illustration at tissue and organ scales.
frame.how: Trace cylinders, bands and nuclei, then inspect the bent arm.
frame.when: Use the illustration to consolidate the preceding explanation.
frame.conditions: Colours are schematic and no process arrow is printed.
frame.atmosphere: Parallel orange fibres beside the upper-arm drawing.

frame.process: Recognise smooth-muscle structure in internal organ walls.
frame.how: Zoom into organ walls and inspect tapering outline, central nucleus and absent bands.
frame.when: Introduce the second muscle-family member.
frame.conditions: Locate the tissue within an organ rather than equating tissue with the whole organ.
frame.atmosphere: Intestine, stomach, eye and vessel lead to spindle-shaped cells.

frame.process: Smooth muscle sustains normal internal activity with fatigue resistance.
frame.how: Relate economical tension maintenance to prolonged internal work.
frame.when: During sustained and repeated organ activity.
frame.conditions: The printed description does not imply unlimited function without energy.
frame.atmosphere: Digestive and vessel-wall activity continues without conscious rest breaks.

skipped_steps.why: No quantitative fatigue measure is supplied.

frame.process: Peristalsis moves contents along a hollow organ.
frame.how: A travelling contraction behind contents and relaxation ahead enable transport.
frame.when: During digestive transport, in a coordinated sequence along the tube.
frame.conditions: An isolated squeeze does not explain directed transport.
frame.atmosphere: Food moves through an intestinal segment.

frame.process: Interpret smooth muscle's appearance and control descriptors.
frame.how: Separate unstriated appearance from involuntary activity.
frame.when: After explaining its structure and peristalsis.
frame.conditions: Involuntary does not mean unstriated in every muscle.
frame.atmosphere: An unbanded intestinal cell beside appearance and control cards.

frame.process: Read the paired smooth-muscle and intestine illustration.
frame.how: Inspect the cell group, its label and the adjacent intestine.
frame.when: Connect the smooth-muscle profile back to its organ setting.
frame.conditions: The diagram is schematic; the label names the cell sketch.
frame.atmosphere: Orange spindle cells with blue central nuclei beside intestinal loops.

frame.process: Recognise cardiac muscle as branched striated cells in the heart wall.
frame.how: Zoom from heart wall to cylindrical segments, branches, nuclei and bands.
frame.when: Introduce the third muscle-family member.
frame.conditions: Connected cells are not one fused cell; one nucleus is the usual introductory pattern.
frame.atmosphere: Heart wall beside a branching tissue network.

frame.process: Cardiac muscle normally sustains repeated work without ordinary fatigue.
frame.how: Connect fatigue resistance with ongoing oxygen-dependent energy supply.
frame.when: Across repeated heartbeats, including during sleep.
frame.conditions: Adequate oxygen and blood supply remain necessary.
frame.atmosphere: Regular heartbeats alongside continuing blood supply.

skipped_steps.why: No numerical endurance limit is supplied.

frame.process: Heart-wall contraction and relaxation support ejection and filling.
frame.how: Contraction develops pressure; relaxation permits refilling.
frame.when: The coordinated phases recur in each heartbeat.
frame.conditions: Continuous circulation requires alternating phases, not continuous squeezing.
frame.atmosphere: A chamber fills and then ejects blood.

frame.process: Cardiac-muscle force supports blood distribution.
frame.how: Trace pressure generation to blood flow and delivery to body cells.
frame.when: Repeatedly during normal circulation.
frame.conditions: Valves help direct flow; vessels carry the pumped blood.
frame.atmosphere: Blood leaves the heart and reaches working tissues.

frame.process: Classify cardiac appearance and control independently.
frame.how: Combine striated appearance with involuntary rhythm.
frame.when: After cardiac structure and pumping are understood.
frame.conditions: Automatic rhythm does not require a conscious instruction for each beat.
frame.atmosphere: A beating heart beside two independent descriptor cards.

frame.process: Read the cardiac tissue and heart illustration.
frame.how: Trace branching fibres, stripes, nuclei and the tissue label.
frame.when: Consolidate the cardiac profile before the full comparison.
frame.conditions: Unlabelled white gaps are not identified heart chambers.
frame.atmosphere: Orange branched tissue beside a red heart.

frame.process: Compare all three muscle types on common criteria.
frame.how: Compare location, function, appearance, nuclei and control side by side.
frame.when: After the three individual profiles.
frame.conditions: Appearance and conscious control must remain separate axes.
frame.atmosphere: A three-column comparison grid with familiar body locations.

frame.process: Identify the three muscle drawings using combined visual evidence.
frame.how: Read skeletal, cardiac and smooth drawings in order.
frame.when: Immediately after the comparison table.
frame.conditions: Use outline, branching, bands and nuclei rather than colour.
frame.atmosphere: Three pink tissue drawings aligned with their table rows.

frame.process: Evaluate the cardiac-tissue statement question.
frame.how: Test striation, voluntary control and shared descriptors independently.
frame.when: After teaching the comparison.
frame.conditions: Answer by statement number because the continuation options are uncertain.
frame.atmosphere: Three exam statements with true or false checks.

frame.process: Select the muscle-to-bone connector.
frame.how: Match tendon, ligament and cartilage with their actual functions.
frame.when: After muscle attachment and movement have been explained.
frame.conditions: A correct tendon option excludes None.
frame.atmosphere: An attachment diagram beside the four answer options.

frame.process: Read a neuron chain and identify the direction of its electrical signal.
frame.how: Follow incoming axon, receiving branches, cell body, outgoing axon and next junction.
frame.when: Introduce the communication pathway after the muscle section.
frame.conditions: Distinct neurons communicate at synapses; the nucleus is not the impulse origin.
frame.atmosphere: The labelled two-neuron diagram with an incoming previous axon.

frame.process: Follow communication through successive neurons.
frame.how: Receive input, initiate an impulse when excitation is sufficient, conduct and transfer at a synapse.
frame.when: Terminal transmission follows impulse arrival.
frame.conditions: An individual input need not generate an output impulse.
frame.atmosphere: A moving highlight follows the diagram and pauses at synaptic junctions.

frame.process: Answer how neurons transmit messages to other cells.
frame.how: Distinguish electrical conduction along the axon from typical chemical synaptic transfer.
frame.when: After the labelled diagram and route walkthrough.
frame.conditions: The chemical account is typical, not universal to all synapses.
frame.atmosphere: The panel question beside an axon and enlarged synapse.

videos.title: Plant tissues का पूरा family tree

frame.process: Classify plant tissues first by active division, then meristems by position and permanent tissues by cell-type composition.
frame.how: Trace parent–child connections, explain each member through structure, role and location, then contrast easily confused branches.
frame.when: Read from the root to major branches, tissue groups, specialised forms and visible transport components; this is not a time sequence.
frame.conditions: Meristematic cells actively divide; permanent cells are differentiated and generally not actively dividing. Simple and complex describe composition.
frame.atmosphere: Picture a growing plant with extending tips, flexible young stalks, hard supporting parts and transport pathways through roots, stems and leaves.

beats.say: पानी वाले पौधे में हवा की जगहें क्यों हों? Aerenchyma, Parenchyma का sponge जैसा रूप है: बड़ी air spaces भीतर gases पहुँचाती हैं और तैरने में भी मदद कर सकती हैं।
beats.on_screen: Aquatic plant → large connected air spaces; trace to Parenchyma.

beats.say: हरा पत्ता खाना कहाँ बनाता है? Chlorenchyma यानी chloroplast वाला Parenchyma। Chlorophyll रोशनी पकड़ता है, जिससे photosynthesis होता है; इसलिए Parenchyma storage, खाना बनाने या air spaces रखने जैसे अलग काम कर सकता है।

beats.voice: हरा पत्ता खाना कहाँ बनाता है? Chlorenchyma यानी chloroplast वाला Parenchyma। Chlorophyll रोशनी पकड़ता है, जिससे photosynthesis होता है; इसलिए Parenchyma storage, खाना बनाने या air spaces रखने जैसे अलग काम कर सकता है।

beats.say: नई डंडी बिना टूटे कैसे मुड़ती है? Collenchyma, Simple tissue का जीवित सदस्य, कोनों पर unevenly thickened दीवारों से लचीला सहारा देता है। पत्ती की डंडी और कई young dicot stems में बाहर के पास मिलता है, जिससे बढ़त बनी रहे।

beats.say: नारियल को कड़ा सहारा कैसे मिलता है? Sclerenchyma यानी मजबूत खोल जैसा Simple tissue। Lignin से मोटी दीवारें कड़ी होती हैं; cells आम तौर पर maturity पर dead होकर भी सहारा देते हैं। इसकी forms Fibres और Sclereids हैं।

beats.say: Pipe के टुकड़े जोड़ो तो क्या बनेगा? Xylem के Vessels, या Tracheae, ऐसे जुड़े elements की नलियाँ हैं। Tracheids से अलग, end walls की openings रास्ता जोड़ती हैं; mature elements dead और खोखले होते हैं।

beats.say: Pipeline के पास छोटा store कौन है? Xylem parenchyma यानी जीवित helper cells, जो सामान जमा करके बगल में पहुँचाते हैं। इसलिए सारा Xylem dead नहीं; helpers और नलियाँ साथ होने से यह Complex है।

beats.say: जाली वाले सिरों की food line कैसी होगी? Sieve tubes, Phloem के जुड़े जीवित elements हैं। Sieve plates के pores से तरल गुजरता है; maturity पर nucleus नहीं रहता, फिर भी helper cells के साथ ये जीवित रहते हैं।

beats.say: Parenchyma आम तौर पर जीवित, thin-walled है; Collenchyma जीवित, uneven thickening से flexible support देता है। Sclerenchyma आम तौर पर maturity पर dead, lignified दीवारों से rigid support देता है; इसके fibers लंबे-पतले, Sclereids अक्सर छोटे, अलग आकार के हैं।

frame.process: Locate three meristem positions and connect them to length or girth growth.
frame.how: Read the whole plant and enlarged insets from shoot tip to leaf base, stem side and root tip.
frame.when: These regions act during plant growth; the diagram is spatial, not a time sequence.
frame.conditions: Interpret arrows as growth directions and bands as schematic position markers.
frame.atmosphere: Picture a young plant becoming taller, extending roots and developing a thicker stem.

frame.process: Examine meristematic cells and the positions that organise their growth effects.
frame.how: Zoom from growing organs to cell outlines and internal compartments, then connect each location with its function.
frame.when: New cells are supplied during growth and can subsequently enlarge and specialise.
frame.conditions: Use several identifying features together; vacuole absence and beneath-bark placement are simplified cues.
frame.atmosphere: Move between a familiar seedling and magnified views of its growing tissues.

frame.process: Explain compact packing and the active cell-production role of meristems.
frame.how: Connect absent between-cell gaps to close packing, and repeated division to new building units.
frame.when: During active growth.
frame.conditions: Between-cell spaces differ from intracellular vacuoles; division is the principal role, not the only cellular activity.
frame.atmosphere: Picture a tightly packed workshop supplying new cells to a growing plant.

frame.process: Compare three tissue–location pairings.
frame.how: Check location, growth effect and restrictive wording side by side.
frame.when: After learning the growth regions and before choosing a statement combination.
frame.conditions: Treat beneath bark as the intended school-level location cue and scrutinise only.
frame.atmosphere: An examination table beside a labelled plant sketch.

frame.process: Select the correct supplied statement combination.
frame.how: Reject statement 1, retain statements 2 and 3, then match the printed options.
frame.when: After checking every statement independently.
frame.conditions: Read the options together with the preceding page's statements.
frame.atmosphere: A statement-combination practice question, with no verified examination provenance.

frame.process: Explain why cells adopt specialised roles and are called permanent.
frame.how: Connect the need for working tissues with specialisation and the usual loss of division.
frame.when: As newly produced cells mature.
frame.conditions: Permanent does not mean dead or absolutely incapable of renewed division.
frame.atmosphere: A growing plant needs completed working parts as well as new cells.

frame.process: Follow differentiation into characteristic shape, size and function.
frame.how: Track a meristem-produced cell through maturation and structural specialisation.
frame.when: After cell production, as daughter cells mature; no fixed interval is supplied.
frame.conditions: Distinguish division, enlargement and differentiation rather than treating them as synonyms.
frame.atmosphere: Follow one young shoot cell into a mature working tissue.

skipped_steps.why: The source supplies no specific differentiation failure mechanism or consequence to teach.

frame.process: Examine vacuole and wall features in mature plant cells.
frame.how: Move from the outer wall toward the central vacuole and connect each feature to its contribution.
frame.when: As cells develop mature structural features.
frame.conditions: Wall thickness varies; a large living vacuolar compartment is not universal in permanent tissues.
frame.atmosphere: A magnified mature living plant cell contrasted with specialised supporting cells.

frame.process: Connect permanent tissues with protection, support, storage and photosynthesis.
frame.how: Map each listed function onto a familiar plant part and explain division of labour.
frame.when: When differentiated tissues perform their specialised roles.
frame.conditions: The functions belong to the tissue family collectively, not necessarily to each cell.
frame.atmosphere: A whole plant with its covering, upright stem, stored food and green leaves.

skipped_steps.why: There is no numerical magnitude requiring a scale comparison.
The supplied fact contains no formula.

beats.say: पौधा लंबा होता है और तना मोटा भी—क्या दोनों की growth एक जगह होती है? Meristematic tissue की जगह देखकर इसका जवाब निकालेंगे, फिर cells का specialised बनना समझेंगे।

videos.title: Simple permanent tissues: खाना जमा करना, मुड़ना और मजबूती

frame.process: Define simple permanent tissue and two parenchyma specialisations.
frame.how: Use cell similarity, chlorophyll and enlarged air spaces as defining criteria.
frame.when: After differentiation; specialisations depend on cell contents and arrangement.
frame.conditions: Chlorophyll distinguishes chlorenchyma; prominent air spaces distinguish aerenchyma.
frame.atmosphere: A green leaf and an aquatic plant beside a simple cell-group drawing.

frame.process: Establish parenchyma functions and its broad distribution.
frame.how: Separate food manufacture from food storage and locate the tissue across organs.
frame.when: Food may be produced and used at different times.
frame.conditions: Photosynthesis requires appropriate living green cells and light.
frame.atmosphere: A whole plant, soft fruit and food-storage tissue.

skipped_steps.why: These are qualitative facts with no numerical quantity to show to scale.

frame.process: Inspect parenchyma cell walls, shapes and packing.
frame.how: Read from the cell boundary to the gaps between neighbouring cells.
frame.when: During identification of a tissue section.
frame.conditions: Cell shapes vary; thin walls and spaces are the combined clues.
frame.atmosphere: A magnified group of soft internal plant cells.

frame.process: Locate collenchyma in leaf stalks and dicot stems.
frame.how: Trace a leaf blade through its stalk into the stem.
frame.when: Where growing parts need flexible support.
frame.conditions: Retain the dicot qualification in the supplied stem location.
frame.atmosphere: A leaf moving in wind.

skipped_steps.why: The occurrence fact has no numerical scale.

frame.process: Inspect living elongated cells with uneven corner reinforcement.
frame.how: Read wall corners, cell interiors and close packing in order.
frame.when: In growing supporting regions.
frame.conditions: Very little intercellular space; thickening is not proof of cell death.
frame.atmosphere: A magnified leaf-stalk section.

frame.process: Explain strength combined with bending.
frame.how: Connect uneven primary-wall reinforcement to flexible support.
frame.when: During wind-driven movement and bending around supports.
frame.conditions: Photosynthesis additionally requires chloroplasts; support does not itself cause tendril coiling.
frame.atmosphere: A bending leaf stalk and a climber on a trellis.

frame.process: Inspect sclerenchyma locations, walls and mature cell status.
frame.how: Move from coconut husk and plant organs to lignified walls and lost living contents.
frame.when: The dead-cell description applies to typical mature sclerenchyma.
frame.conditions: Long narrow shape particularly describes fibres, not every sclerenchyma form.
frame.atmosphere: Coconut fibres, a leaf vein and a hard seed covering.

frame.process: Explain rigid strength, protection and reduction of the lumen.
frame.how: Wall deposition reinforces the framework while narrowing its interior.
frame.when: As secondary walls thicken and the support tissue matures.
frame.conditions: A narrow lumen may remain; complete cavity absence is not universal.
frame.atmosphere: A thick-walled cell beside a protective seed covering.

frame.process: Read the two supplied comparative tissue figures.
frame.how: Follow left-to-right labels, views, wall layers and spaces.
frame.when: After learning the tissues and before comparing table criteria.
frame.conditions: Adjacent drawings are comparisons, not conversion stages; printed colour is not physiological evidence.
frame.atmosphere: Two enlarged tissue plates with traced leader lines.

frame.process: Compare all three tissues across the eight table criteria.
frame.how: Read each criterion across all three columns and connect differences to function.
frame.when: After visual identification.
frame.conditions: Qualify living status by maturity, photosynthesis by chloroplasts, and broad occurrence claims by textbook context.
frame.atmosphere: A growing comparison table beside a stem landmark drawing.

frame.process: Test three proposed tissue–feature matches.
frame.how: Check each match against walls, living contents and functions.
frame.when: After the reference comparison is established.
frame.conditions: Mechanical strength in climbers does not uniquely identify one tissue.
frame.atmosphere: Three statement cards beside the reference table.

frame.process: Answer the statement-combination, lignin and buoyancy questions.
frame.how: Identify decisive clues, eliminate distractors and flag ambiguous wording.
frame.when: At the end of the lesson.
frame.conditions: The combination answer is apparently intended, not logically unambiguous.
frame.atmosphere: Book practice questions with highlighted keywords.

frame.process: Complex tissue combines different cell types; xylem combines conducting, storage and supporting components.
frame.how: Read the tissue assembly, then its four components and the walls and interiors of its conducting elements.
frame.when: Mature conducting elements are distinguished from developing cells.
frame.conditions: An open conducting space and reinforced walls support conduction; living parenchyma qualifies whole-tissue dead-cell claims.
frame.atmosphere: Picture a stem transport network with conduits, neighbouring storage cells and reinforcing fibres.

frame.process: Complex tissues distribute supplies; xylem combines vertical conduction, sideways transfer, storage and support.
frame.how: Connect separated supply and demand locations to tubular conducting elements, parenchyma and fibres.
frame.when: Supplies move as plant parts require them; the explanation follows need, route and associated functions.
frame.conditions: Tube shape provides a route, not the complete force driving upward movement.
frame.atmosphere: Follow water from roots through a stem, then toward neighbouring tissues.

frame.process: Complex permanent tissues are grouped as xylem and phloem.
frame.how: Distinguish their principal cargo while retaining their shared organisation of cooperating cell types.
frame.when: Introduce the family before studying individual components.
frame.conditions: The division concerns tissue identity and principal transport role, not identical cells.
frame.atmosphere: Picture parallel water-supply and food-distribution networks in one plant.

frame.process: Phloem includes five named component types with different roles.
frame.how: Move from conducting cells to companion cells, fibres and parenchyma, then compare their jobs.
frame.when: Read this as a general component list, not compulsory coexistence of all five in every plant.
frame.conditions: Sieve cells and sieve tubes are different conducting forms.
frame.atmosphere: Zoom into food-conducting tissue in a stem.

frame.process: Sieve-tube elements form a food-conducting tube with perforated connecting end regions.
frame.how: Zoom from phloem to the tube, its element walls and sieve plates.
frame.when: Successive elements connect along the conducting route.
frame.conditions: Perforated does not mean unrestricted holes throughout every wall.
frame.atmosphere: Imagine joined pipe sections with sieve-like connecting plates.

frame.process: Phloem distributes leaf-made food and is living apart from the stated fibre exception.
frame.how: State each fact, locate its supporting text and explain its consequence.
frame.when: Food goes to consuming or storage regions; mature fibres are the living-cell exception.
frame.conditions: Neither downward-only transport nor all-cells-living is a valid absolute.
frame.atmosphere: Follow food from a leaf toward growing plant parts.

skipped_steps.why: These are qualitative facts without a numerical quantity to show to scale.

frame.process: The drawings identify whole-tissue components and enlarged conducting-cell details.
frame.how: Read the upper pair left to right, then the lower isolated and grouped xylem and phloem views.
frame.when: Move from the overview to individual elements and their grouped arrangement.
frame.conditions: Leader lines identify parts, colours are illustrative, and an unclear pointer cannot establish an exact target.
frame.atmosphere: Inspect labelled drawings as identification evidence rather than flow diagrams.

frame.process: Compare xylem and phloem across cargo, living condition, walls, permeability, materials and support.
frame.how: Take one criterion at a time and explain the limits of the printed shorthand.
frame.when: Compare after both component families and their drawings are understood.
frame.conditions: Component-level exceptions prevent absolute interpretations of the table.
frame.atmosphere: Place the two transport networks side by side in the same plant.

frame.process: A stem region is enlarged to locate xylem, cambium and phloem and show transport arrows.
frame.how: Read outer landmarks, centre, vascular positions and then the magnified longitudinal view.
frame.when: The red arrow changes viewing scale; black arrows depict movement.
frame.conditions: The arrangement belongs to the illustrated stem; downward phloem arrows are not a universal direction rule.
frame.atmosphere: Zoom from a stem segment into its conducting region.

frame.process: Identify the option that does not belong to xylem.
frame.how: Read except, classify each option and explain why parenchyma remains a valid xylem component.
frame.when: Attempt after learning both tissue families.
frame.conditions: Shared transport functions do not imply shared component membership.
frame.atmosphere: A supplied multiple-choice practice question; no examination provenance is assumed.

beats.say: Coconut husk के मजबूत fibres देखे हैं? Sclerenchyma ऐसा supporting tissue है; mature cells की walls मोटी, lignin से कड़ी और आम तौर पर living contents के बिना होती हैं। ये मजबूती देती हैं, waxy covering नहीं बनातीं। इसलिए option a केवल ‘मोटा’ शब्द से सही नहीं होगा।

beats.say: Potato के अंदर खाना कहाँ जमा रहता है? उसके storage tissue में Parenchyma मिलता है, यानी आम तौर पर पतली walls वाली living cells का tissue। यह storage करता है; इसके specialised रूप photosynthesis भी करते हैं। यहाँ clue बाहरी waxy covering का है, storage का नहीं; इसलिए c हटेगा।

beats.say: Gases concentration के फर्क से diffusion करती हैं; photosynthesis के लिए carbon dioxide अंदर आ सकती है और oxygen बाहर जा सकती है। Photosynthesis और respiration के लिए exchange चाहिए, मगर इसी रास्ते water vapour भी निकल सकती है। कई जमीन वाले broad leaves में नीचे अधिक stomata होते हैं, लेकिन यह हर leaf का नियम नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: CO₂ inward; O₂ and water vapour outward; distribution varies among leaves.

beats.say: इस छेद के दोनों ओर कौन है? Guard cells की जोड़ी, यानी opening खोलने-बंद करने वाली specialised epidermal cells। पानी की मात्रा और अंदर का pressure, यानी turgor, बदलने से इनका आकार बदलता है। दरवाजे जैसी ये cells रास्ता संभालती हैं; gases बीच के pore से गुजरती हैं, इसलिए a नहीं चुनेंगे।

beats.say: पानी में उगते पौधे के अंदर sponge जैसी बड़ी खाली जगहें किस काम आती हैं? Aerenchyma, specialised Parenchyma है जिसमें बड़े air spaces होते हैं। Water hyacinth जैसे पौधों में ये अंदर gases पहुँचाने और तैरने में मदद करते हैं। लेकिन अंदर के air spaces, leaf के बाहर का pore नहीं हैं; इसलिए c गलत है।
beats.on_screen: Aquatic plant → internal air spaces → gas movement and buoyancy; not a surface pore.

beats.say: हरी पत्ती के अंदर खाना बनाने वाला tissue कौन-सा है? Chlorenchyma, यानी chloroplasts वाला Parenchyma; chloroplasts रोशनी की मदद से खाना बनाने का काम करते हैं। यह carbon dioxide इस्तेमाल करता है, जबकि Stomata उसके आने का रास्ता हैं। इसलिए d भी नहीं; दूसरे question का intended answer b, Stomata है।
beats.on_screen: Stomatal pore: entry → Chlorenchyma: photosynthesis. Intended answer: b.

beats.say: Options अलग रखने की trick है: layer, material, opening या काम? Epidermis layer है, Suberin material; Stomata opening हैं, Guard cells उसके controllers। Sclerenchyma मजबूती, Parenchyma storage, Aerenchyma air spaces और Chlorenchyma photosynthesis से जोड़ो। केवल protection या gas शब्द मिलना काफी नहीं है।
